headline: EU Chief Backs Slower Frontier AI Development and New Child Social-Media Limits
seoTitle: EU Backs Slower Frontier AI, Child Social-Media Limits | FMB Worldwide
seoDescription: EU Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen backed slowing frontier AI development and proposed new social-media restrictions for children.
deck: Europe is pushing simultaneously on frontier-AI risk and children’s access to social media, with potential effects beyond the EU.
author: FMB Worldwide

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen backed efforts to slow frontier AI development and proposed stricter social-media access rules for children during her September 16 State of the Union address.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Reuters reported that von der Leyen plans talks with leading frontier AI labs. Associated Press reported proposed EU-wide restrictions including a ban for children under 13 and monitored limited accounts for ages 13 to 15. The measures are proposals, not enacted law.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: EU technology rules can influence global platform design and compliance practices that affect Philippine users, BPO firms, schools and regulators.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The AI talks are not a binding pause and the child-access rules still require detailed legislation and political approval.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch detailed legislation, technology-company responses and whether frontier AI labs agree to common evaluation or pacing measures.
